changelog:
The software factory: /run-todo and /do now prove every story done before it is committed.

Features: each acceptance criterion can carry a `verify:` command; ac-verify records a red run before implementation, freezes the story's test files and bindings, and re-runs every binding itself (a run where no test passed is never met). ship-check seals the exact gated code and its records, and `commit.js --ship-check` refuses a commit when code, a frozen test, a binding or an earlier story's baseline changed after the seal, when the seal and commit name different stories, or when the wave review is missing. plan-check derives waves from dependencies, lists overlapping writers (they run in separate worktrees from local HEAD), validates the plan and orders later-slice stories after a Ship gate that waits for the owner's go. A failure ledger stops a third identical gate failure (the second gets one deep-tier retry), and a Budget line caps attempts, gate failures, dispatches and minutes per run. run-record, run-trace and a scoreboard measure each run; a scheduled detect-only job can run the gate and file an intake note when it is red; the improvement loop (issue log, intake, verdict, protected set) applies only behind owner review. /todo, /run-todo and /do share one review cadence. fleet sync --adopter syncs one project. Skill profiles: fail-closed profiles, role allow-lists and leaner workflows.

Fixes: twelve frictions from the first real adopter run (path aliases and wave-wide modules in red runs, nested package-manager name filters, manual-only stories, root CLAUDE.md in --docs, dispatch counting and more).

Migration: none required. Stories without `verify:` lines still run; add them through /todo to get the proof. Write a wave's tests only when that wave starts.

--- v6.14 ---
Secret scanner: a moved, renamed or byte-identical copy of content that is already committed (or already on the remote) is no longer rescanned at commit or push, so moving a folder no longer re-raises old false positives. Any changed byte is still a new blob and is scanned.

--- v6.13 ---
Memory servers as a fallback chain, and memories without metadata index on Node 24.

Features: MEMORY_EMBED_URL and MEMORY_CAPTURE_BASE_URL take several servers, comma-separated, best machine first (for example three Ollama hosts on a Tailscale network). Each call tries them in order within one time budget (400 ms for a prompt's recall); a server that is refused, unreachable or missing the model is tried last for the next 2 minutes, so a machine that is off costs at most one slow prompt, while a cold model load inside a prompt's budget is not counted as a failure. memory-capture.js status shows the chain and any recent failure. Every listed server must carry the same embedding model.

Fixes: a memory with no metadata or content no longer fails to index on Node 24 (node:sqlite refuses an undefined bind; Node 26 hid it by storing NULL).

Migration: none required. A single MEMORY_EMBED_URL keeps working as before. To serve other machines, Ollama must listen beyond loopback (OLLAMA_HOST); expose it on the Tailscale interface only, since Ollama has no authentication.
